newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed on profit taking after new high.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed on profit taking after new high.

text.p: Profit taking in a shortened post-holiday trading session continued to weigh on CME hog futures after December posted a new contract high early. Pork bellies remained sharply higher on fundamental and technical demand, traders said.

December hogs posted a new contract high of 59.575 cents a lb and then slipped to close 0.075 lower at 59.150 cents. Lean months finished up 0.325 to off 0.375 cent. Bellies ended 1.725 to 0.450 higher with February up most at 81.100 cents.
Profit taking developed in hog futures after December climbed to a new high early.

The continued firm tone to cash hogs and growing weather concerns from storm fronts moving up from the southwest provided the bulk of early support before the profit taking developed. The market also looked technically strong after the rally earlier in the week, traders said.

Scattered local and commission house buying gave way to general profit taking in December. Rand Financials sold February after the early advance. In hog options, ADM Investor Services sold December 58 calls, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures also encountered profit taking after the jump to highest levels since late August but renewed buying and market-on-close buy orders boosted prices again by the close. Technical as well as fundamental factors pushed prices up, traders said.

A continued stronger-than-expected tone to cash bellies provided the bulk of fundamental demand. Cash bellies were quoted by USDA $1 to $3 per cwt higher Friday morning, with 12- to 14-lb supplies quoted at $70.00 to $71.00 and 14- to 16-lb bellies quoted at $72.00 to $73.00.

The gains put belly values at highest levels since October 4, much higher than had been expected to this time of year, traders said. Demand for product remains good and storage stocks are low, they said.

Technically, the market also looked stronger, especially after breaking through chart resistance around the 80.000 cent area in February, sources noted. The close above 81.000 cents indicated futures may move up to a new contract high of 89.750 or better in February, chartists said.
Both contracts closed early at 1200 CST/1800 GMT in continued observance of the Thanksgiving holiday.
